newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel to review European stakes - paper.
newsitem.headline: SingTel to review European stakes - paper.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) wants to invest in the Asia-Pacific region in the future and will review its European shareholdings, the Straits Times newspaper said on Monday.

The newspaper quoted Allen Lew, the head of SingTel's overseas investment arm Singapore Telecom International (STI), as saying the company's Singapore $900 million (US$640 million) investment in Belgian telephone operator Belgacom would be SingTel's last in Europe.
In December 1995, SingTel, Ameritech of the United States and Tele Danmark jointly paid US$2.47 billion for almost 50 percent of the Belgian monopoly.
Lew said any new deals in Europe would be done through Belgacom.

"From now on, we will focus all our overseas efforts on the Asia Pacific region. With the exception of Belgacom, we will probably not be going out of the Asia-Pacific region," the newspaper quoted Lew as saying in an interview.
"Since our focus is now shifted to the Asia-Pacific, when the time is right, we will look at what to do with our European shareholdings," he said.

SingTel currently has a 19.7 percent stake in Norwegian cellular telecommuniations firm NetCom GSM, a nine percent stake in Britain's General Cable as well as investments in Swedish cable television Stjarn TV.

"Our primary goal in Sweden is to see how we can grow the company. That could result in either us divesting or reducing our stake if we don't figure prominently in (Stjarn TV's) plans. We are still talking to several people concerning Stjarn," Lew said.
"Our focus on the Asia-Pacific means that we would not be aggressively pursuing opportunities nor embarking on strong business development efforts outside of the Asia Pacific."
"As for the existing investments...we will continue to uphold our commitment to them as long as we continue to hold stakes in them," the newspaper quoted Lew as saying.
He said SingTel wanted its future overseas investments to yield large profits in line with its aim of getting 20 percent of group profits from foreign stakeholdings.

"We have to do more Belgacom-type deals (in Asia) where the impact -- the equity accounted profits -- are closer to the S$100-150 million range instead of being in the S$10-20 million range," he said.
Company officials were unavailable to comment on the report.
